read.sections.0.text.source:
A history painting presents an account of the past through figures, setting and arrangement. Its artist chooses which moment to show and whose actions seem important. Two paintings of Prince Diponegoro's capture show how such choices can support power. They can also challenge its public image. The pictures also have histories of their own. Later audiences can give them meanings that their first viewers would not have shared.

Diponegoro was a Javanese prince and a major leader of resistance during the Java War of 1825–1830. Dutch colonial authorities sought to control Java, where local rulers and communities had their own interests. Colonial rule means control of a territory by an outside power. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro was arrested at Magelang during talks. He had been given a promise of safe conduct: a promise that he could come and go safely. The arrest helped bring the war to an end. It happened in the Dutch East Indies, long before Indonesia proclaimed its independence in 1945.
read.sections.0.text.back:
A history painting presents an account of the past through figures, setting and arrangement. Its artist chooses which moment will be shown and whose actions seem important. Two paintings of Prince Diponegoro's arrest show how such choices can support power. Those choices can also challenge the image of power in the public's eyes. The paintings also have their own histories. Later audiences can give them meanings that their first audiences would not have had.

Diponegoro was a Javanese prince and one of the main leaders of resistance in the Java War of 1825–1830. The Dutch colonial government tried to control Java, where local rulers and communities had their own interests. Colonial rule means control over a territory by a power from outside. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro was arrested in Magelang during negotiations. He had been given a guarantee of safety: a promise that he could come and go safely. The arrest helped end the war. This event happened in the Dutch East Indies, long before Indonesia proclaimed its independence in 1945.
read.sections.0.text.note: "capture" is "penangkapan" (arrest), as in Saleh's Indonesian title. "safe conduct" is "jaminan keamanan". "talks" is "perundingan", as Southeast Asia's TERMS.

read.sections.0.simpler.source:
A history painting tells a story about the past. The artist picks one moment and who looks important. Two paintings show the capture of Prince Diponegoro. Art can back up power or question it. Later, people gave the paintings new meanings.

Diponegoro was a prince from Java. He led a fight against Dutch control in the Java War, from 1825 to 1830. Colonial rule means rule of a land by an outside power. Dutch officials wanted to rule Java. But the rulers and people of Java had their own goals. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro came to Magelang for talks. The Dutch had promised he would be safe. But they arrested him. This helped end the war. Then, the land was called the Dutch East Indies. Indonesia became free much later, in 1945.
read.sections.0.simpler.back:
A history painting tells about the past. Its artist chooses one moment and who looks important. Two paintings show the arrest of Prince Diponegoro. Art can support power or question it. Later, people gave the paintings new meanings.

Diponegoro was a prince from Java. He led resistance against Dutch rule in the Java War, from 1825 to 1830. Colonial rule means a land is governed by a power from outside. Dutch officials wanted to control Java. But the rulers and people of Java had their own goals. On 28 March 1830, Diponegoro came to Magelang to negotiate. The Dutch had promised he would be safe. But they arrested him. This helped end the war. At that time, this land was called the Dutch East Indies. Indonesia became independent much later, in 1945.

read.sections.1.text.source:
The Dutch artist Nicolaas Pieneman painted his version around 1830–1835. It was a commission for General Hendrik Merkus de Kock. He was the officer who ordered the arrest. Its familiar title, The Submission of Prince Dipo Negoro to General De Kock, encourages viewers to see the scene as a surrender. Upright Dutch officers, the raised Dutch flag and followers gathered below make colonial authority look certain. The commission matters: this was an account made for the victorious commander.

Raden Saleh completed The Arrest of Prince Diponegoro in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He built his painting career through training and patronage in Europe. He worked across connected but unequal worlds. Both praise in Europe and his ties to his homeland shaped his career. His life does not fit a simple split between a European way of painting and a separate Javanese view. Oil painting could carry an account that questioned colonial power.
read.sections.1.text.back:
The Dutch artist Nicolaas Pieneman painted his version around 1830–1835. That painting was a commission for General Hendrik Merkus de Kock. He was the officer who ordered the arrest. Its well-known title, The Submission of Prince Dipo Negoro to General De Kock (The Surrender of Prince Dipo Negoro to General De Kock), encourages people looking at it to treat the scene as a surrender. The Dutch officers standing upright, the Dutch flag flying high and the followers gathered below make colonial power look certain. The commission matters: this is an account made for the commander who won.

Raden Saleh completed The Arrest of Prince Diponegoro in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He built his career as a painter through training and the support of patrons in Europe. He worked between worlds that were connected but not equal. Praise in Europe and his ties to his birthplace both shaped his career. His life does not fit a simple division between a European way of painting and a separate Javanese view. Oil painting could carry an account that questioned colonial power.
read.sections.1.text.note: Saleh's painting is called by its Indonesian title in the reading, as Indonesian learners know it. "commission" is "pesanan", the glossary word, with the forms used in Lesson 11 ("memesan", "dipesan").

read.sections.1.simpler.source:
A Dutch artist, Nicolaas Pieneman, painted his version in about 1830 to 1835. It was a commission from General De Kock. He ordered the arrest. A commission is a request to make a work. The title calls the scene a submission. That means giving up. Dutch officers stand tall. A Dutch flag flies high. His followers are lower down. So Dutch power looks sure and strong. The painting was made for the winner.

Raden Saleh finished his painting in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He trained in Europe, and people there paid for his art. He lived between two worlds that were not equal. He won praise in Europe, but he felt close to his home. So we cannot just call his art Dutch or Javanese. His oil painting could question Dutch power.
read.sections.1.simpler.back:
A Dutch artist, Nicolaas Pieneman, painted his version around 1830 to 1835. That painting was a commission from General De Kock. He was the one who ordered the arrest. A commission is a request to make a work. Its title calls the scene a submission. That means giving up. The Dutch officers stand upright. The Dutch flag flies high. Diponegoro's followers are below. So Dutch power looks certain and strong. The painting was made for the side that won.

Raden Saleh completed his painting in 1857. Saleh came from Java. He studied in Europe, and people there paid for his art. He lived between two worlds that were not equal. He was praised in Europe, but he felt close to his birthplace. So we cannot simply call his art Dutch or Javanese. His oil painting could question Dutch power.
read.sections.1.simpler.note: "It was a commission from General De Kock": the English simpler says "from"; the standard text says "for". Both are kept as in English.

read.sections.2.text.source:
In Saleh's composition, Diponegoro stands upright near De Kock, surrounded by distressed followers. His white clothing and firm posture give him dignity at the moment of capture. The crowd brings the emotional cost of the arrest into the foreground. Unlike Pieneman, Saleh includes no flying Dutch flag. These differences help explain why scholars see the later painting as a challenge to the earlier one. That reading connects visible choices with historical context. A painted face alone cannot prove what a person actually felt.

The painting's later life matters too. The Dutch government returned Saleh's work to Indonesia in 1978. Diponegoro's image has appeared on posters, monuments and other artworks. It has helped later generations debate heroism, resistance and national identity. National identity means the ideas and memories through which people feel they belong to a nation. Such uses belong to Indonesia's changing history. They do not prove that Saleh held every later nationalist belief. Neither painting speaks for every Dutch or Javanese person. Neither gives a complete, neutral history of the war. Together, they show how art takes part in struggles over whose account becomes public memory.
read.sections.2.text.back:
In Saleh's composition, Diponegoro stands upright near De Kock, surrounded by grieving followers. His white clothing and his firm posture give him dignity at the moment he is arrested. The crowd brings the emotional burden of the arrest into the foreground. Unlike Pieneman, Saleh does not show a flying Dutch flag. These differences help explain why experts see the later painting as a challenge to the earlier painting. That reading connects visible choices with their historical context. A painted face alone cannot prove what a person really felt.

The painting's life in later times matters too. The Dutch government returned Saleh's work to Indonesia in 1978. Diponegoro's image has appeared on posters, monuments and other artworks. That image has helped later generations debate heroism, resistance and national identity. National identity means the ideas and memories that make people feel they are part of a nation. Uses like these belong to Indonesia's history, which keeps changing. Those uses do not prove that Saleh held every national belief that appeared later. Neither of the two paintings represents every Dutch person or Javanese person. Neither gives a complete and neutral history of the war. Together, the two show how art takes part in struggles over whose account becomes public memory.
read.sections.2.text.note: "distressed followers" is "para pengikut yang bersedih" (grieving); "yang gelisah" (anxious) is closer to "distressed". "nationalist" is "kebangsaan" (national), less loaded than "nasionalis" for young readers; reviewers decide.

read.sections.2.simpler.source:
Saleh's composition is different. A composition is how the parts of a picture are arranged. The prince stands tall near De Kock. He wears white. The men and women around him are upset. This gives him dignity, even as he is caught. The crowd shows how painful the arrest was. Saleh's painting has no Dutch flag. So experts say it pushes back against Pieneman's story. But a painted face cannot prove what a real person felt.

Later, in 1978, the Dutch government gave it back to Indonesia. The prince's picture has been on posters and statues. People use it to talk about heroes and the fight for freedom. They also talk about national identity. That means the ideas that make people feel part of a nation. This does not prove what Saleh believed. Neither painting speaks for all Dutch or all Javanese people. Neither tells the whole story of the war. People still argue about whose story is remembered.
read.sections.2.simpler.back:
Saleh's composition is different. A composition is the way the parts of a picture are arranged. The prince stands upright near De Kock. He is dressed in white. The men and women around him are sad. This gives him dignity, even though he is being arrested. The crowd shows how painful the arrest was. Saleh's painting has no Dutch flag. So experts say this painting pushes back against Pieneman's story. But a painted face cannot prove what the real person felt.

Later, in 1978, the Dutch government returned it to Indonesia. The prince's image has been on posters and statues. People use it to talk about heroes and the struggle for independence. They also talk about national identity. That means the ideas that make people feel part of a nation. This does not prove what Saleh believed. Neither of the paintings represents all Dutch people or all Javanese people. Neither tells the whole story of that war. People still debate whose story is remembered.

write.prompt.source: In two or three sentences, explain how one difference between these paintings changes the story of the arrest. Say who a painting was made by or for.
write.prompt.back: In two or three sentences, explain how one difference between these two paintings changes the story of the arrest. Say by whom or for whom a painting was made.

write.example.source: In Pieneman's painting, Dutch officers stand tall under a Dutch flag. The prince's followers are lower down. Pieneman painted it for General De Kock, who ordered the arrest. So the scene looks like a surrender. In Saleh's painting, there is no Dutch flag, and the prince stands tall in white. This matters because it gives him dignity. It also shows the arrest as a painful moment for his followers.
write.example.back: In Pieneman's painting, the Dutch officers stand upright under the Dutch flag. The prince's followers are below. Pieneman painted it for General De Kock, who ordered the arrest. So the scene looks like a surrender. In Saleh's painting, there is no Dutch flag, and the prince stands upright dressed in white. This matters because it gives him dignity. The painting also shows the arrest as a painful moment for his followers.

visual.alt.source: Oil painting. Prince Diponegoro, in white, stands at the top of the steps of a veranda on the same level as Dutch officers, one of whom gestures toward a waiting carriage. His followers crowd the steps and ground below, some kneeling and one woman clinging to him, with mountains in the distance.
visual.alt.back: Oil painting. Prince Diponegoro, dressed in white, stands at the top of the steps of a veranda, at the same height as the Dutch officers; one of them points toward a carriage that is waiting. His followers fill the steps and the ground below, some kneeling and a woman holding him tightly, with mountains in the distance.

sensitiveNotes.0.source: Colonial conquest and war: teach colonial rule as an unequal relationship of power. Keep the arrest and the war non-graphic, with no reenactment or role-play. Keep the documented breach of safe conduct (Diponegoro was arrested during negotiations despite a promise of safe conduct) apart from interpretations of poses and faces. Don't describe the Java War as a conflict between two modern nation-states: in 1830 Java was part of the Dutch East Indies, and Indonesia proclaimed independence in 1945.
sensitiveNotes.0.back: Colonial conquest and war: teach colonial rule as an unequal relationship of power. Tell about the arrest and the war without violent detail, without acting out or role-play. Keep the recorded breach of the guarantee of safety (Diponegoro was arrested during negotiations even though he had been promised a guarantee of safety) apart from interpretations of poses and facial expressions. Don't describe the Java War as a conflict between two modern nation-states: in 1830 Java was part of the Dutch East Indies, and Indonesia proclaimed its independence in 1945.

sensitiveNotes.1.source: Identity and belief: Diponegoro was also an Islamic religious leader. No learner is asked to speak for his faith or community, to share their own religion, identity or family, or to represent Indonesians, Javanese or Dutch people. For many learners in Indonesia, Diponegoro is a national hero; treat that later memory as real history to learn about, while keeping it apart from what the 1830 sources show. Accept reasoned answers about either painting without requiring a feeling about it.
sensitiveNotes.1.back: Identity and belief: Diponegoro was also a leader of the Islamic religion. No learner is asked to speak on behalf of his faith or community, to tell about their own religion, identity or family, or to represent Indonesians, Javanese or Dutch people. For many learners in Indonesia, Diponegoro is a national hero; treat that later memory as real history worth learning about, while keeping it apart from what the 1830 sources show. Accept reasoned answers about either painting without requiring a particular feeling about it.

educatorNotes.0.source: Don't use Saleh's European training to dismiss his viewpoint, or assume that his Javanese origins make every detail of his painting factual. Later nationalist readings of the painting and Saleh's own intentions are separate questions; the reading keeps them apart.
educatorNotes.0.back: Don't use Saleh's training in Europe to dismiss his point of view, or assume that his Javanese origins make every detail of his painting factual. Later national readings of the painting and Saleh's own intentions are two separate questions; the reading keeps the two apart.

educatorNotes.2.source: Sources: the Rijksmuseum record gives Pieneman's commission, the safe conduct, the current title and the date range c. 1830–c. 1835 (some older records say 1835). Elly Kent's article (National Gallery Singapore) supports the missing flag, the scholars' reading and the later uses. The Cabinet Secretariat page supports the capture place and date, the 1857 date and the 1978 return; the lesson does not adopt its claims that particular colours prove one intention, or its incorrect claim that Islam forbids all fighting during Ramadan, and its photographs are not used. The 1945 proclamation is from the State Secretariat (setneg.go.id).
educatorNotes.2.back: Sources: the Rijksmuseum record gives Pieneman's commission, the guarantee of safety, the current title and the date range around 1830–around 1835 (some old records say 1835). Elly Kent's article (National Gallery Singapore) supports the point about the flag that isn't there, the experts' reading and the later uses of the painting. The Cabinet Secretariat page supports the place and date of the arrest, the 1857 date and the 1978 return; this lesson does not use its claim that particular colours prove one intention, or its incorrect claim that Islam forbids all fighting during Ramadan, and its photographs are not used. The 1945 proclamation comes from the Ministry of State Secretariat (setneg.go.id).
educatorNotes.2.note: "State Secretariat" is given its full Indonesian name, Kementerian Sekretariat Negara.

educatorNotes.3.source: Images: both are Wikimedia Commons' faithful reproductions of two-dimensional public-domain paintings (Saleh died in 1880, Pieneman in 1860), so the credit links the exact Commons file pages, where the rights statements are. Indonesian sources place Saleh's painting at the Yogyakarta Presidential Palace and at Istana Negara, Jakarta: one work, so the caption gives no fixed display place. Commons reports a heritage registration, RNCB.20190219.01.001562, which is not a museum accession number. Don't swap in the separate "Rijksmuseum Official" Commons file of Pieneman's painting, which carries a CC BY 3.0 statement.
